question: is there any armed walk or run available, and what does the Synty rig have that ours lacks?

synty.armed_locomotion_note: ZERO. sword-combat has Idle / Attack / Block / Dodge / Hit / Death and NO Walk, Run, Strafe or Sprint folder at all (grep over all 243 filenames: 0 hits). base-locomotion is entirely unarmed (Feminine / Masculine / Neutral). No filename in any pack outside sword-combat mentions a weapon.

has_that_we_lack: fingers: Thumb_01..03, IndexFinger_01..04, Finger_01..04 per hand
Prop_L and Prop_R -- DEDICATED WEAPON SOCKET BONES
rig.prop_bones_significance: Synty authored these clips with explicit weapon attachment points, so the sword's intended position AND ORIENTATION per frame is in the data. That is a better source for weapon carry than any wrist heuristic -- it is the animator's own answer to the question Matt is asking.

armed_locomotion: Sword and Shield Alert Turn Left
Sword and Shield Alert Turn Right
axe_attacks: Right-hand Sword Slash (the current attack clip)
meshy.no_straight_armed_run: nothing in either source is a straight armed RUN. Meshy's armed run entries are diagonals (ForwardLeft / ForwardRight Run Fight).
meshy.cost_note: fetching any of these spends Meshy credits; the QUERY was free. Not fetched.

conclusion: Synty cannot supply armed locomotion and Meshy partly can. So walk and run had to be solved by correcting the existing unarmed clips (walk_armed / run_armed), which is what was built. Synty is the right source for the CLIPS WE LACK -- block, parry, dodge, hit, death, armed idle -- and its Prop_R bone is the right source for the axe's carry orientation.
